plain.text: Agrippa gave Paul permission to speak. Paul said he was glad to defend himself before the king, who knew Jewish customs well. He had lived as a strict Pharisee. Now he was on trial because of his hope in what God promised their ancestors. "Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?" He described how he had opposed the name of Jesus, imprisoning and voting against believers, and pursuing them to foreign cities. On the way to Damascus at noon, he saw a light from heaven brighter than the sun and heard a voice in Aramaic: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads." "Who are you, Lord?" "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. Now get up. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and witness, to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins." Paul was not disobedient to the vision. He preached that people should repent, turn to God and show it by their deeds. He was saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said: that the Messiah would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.

Festus interrupted: "You are out of your mind, Paul! Your great learning is driving you insane." Paul replied, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus. What I am saying is true and reasonable. The king knows about these things; it was not done in a corner." "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do." Agrippa said, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?" Paul replied, "Short time or long, I pray to God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains." The officials agreed that Paul had done nothing deserving death or prison. Agrippa said, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."

summary.bigIdea: Paul tells King Agrippa the story of his encounter with Jesus and prays that everyone listening would believe.
points: Paul asks, "Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?"
Jesus sent Paul to turn people "from darkness to light".
Paul hopes all his listeners will become followers of Jesus; the officials agree he is innocent.
summary.reflection: Paul said what happened to Jesus "was not done in a corner". Why do you think he stressed that it was public?
